title: urlToTxtPath diverges from urlToFilename causing ENOENT for non-ASCII URLs
description:
The crawler writes .txt files using urlToFilename() which transliterates non-ASCII characters via unidecode and replaces special chars with hyphens. Example: /café/page.html → cafe/page.txt.

The sync module uses its own urlToTxtPath() which does NOT transliterate and preserves special characters. It looks for café/page.txt which does not exist.

Consequence: for any URL containing accents, special characters, or non-ASCII text, sync throws ENOENT and marks the row sync_status='error'. The .txt file is never uploaded to Drive.
acceptance_criteria:
A shared urlToFilename function exists in @full-content-inventory/shared and is imported by both crawl.ts and sync.ts
sync.ts uses the shared urlToFilename instead of urlToTxtPath
The shared function is tested for accent transliteration, special-char replacement, and index path normalization
All existing tests pass; TypeScript build clean
notes: Fix: (1) Extract urlToFilename from crawl.ts into shared/src/path-utils.ts (or similar). (2) Export it from shared/src/index.ts. (3) Update crawl.ts to import and use the shared version. (4) Delete urlToTxtPath from sync.ts and replace with the shared urlToFilename. (5) Add unit tests for the shared function.
close_reason: Fixed: urlToFilename extracted to shared package, crawl.ts and sync.ts both import it. urlToTxtPath deleted. Tests 28/28 pass, build clean.

title: sync.ts discards rows with empty crawl_status, skipping all txt uploads
description:
The sync() orchestrator in sync.ts filters rows with:

When _inventory.csv was produced before the crawl_status fix (crawler-002) or by any external tool, csv-parse reads the empty crawl_status cell as ''. The strict === 'done' comparison drops every row.

Consequence: rowsToProcess is empty, folderTree is empty, no Drive folders are created, no .txt files are uploaded. Only Step 7 (inventory-as-Sheet upload) runs — which matches the observed symptom of 'only _inventory.csv is uploaded'.

title: gws drive files create --upload fails on absolute paths outside cwd
description:
The gws-sync module's drive.ts functions (uploadAsDoc, uploadAsSheet, updateSheet) all pass absolute file paths to the gws CLI via the --upload flag. However, gws has a security validation that rejects --upload paths outside the current working directory with:

  error[validation]: --upload '/absolute/path/to/file' resolves to '/absolute/path/to/file' which is outside the current directory

This causes the sync to fail entirely when the inventory path points to a directory other than the current working directory (which is always the case in practice, since crawls write to ~/tmp/...).
acceptance_criteria:
uploadAsDoc succeeds when given an absolute path outside cwd
uploadAsSheet succeeds when given an absolute path outside cwd
updateSheet succeeds when given an absolute path outside cwd
All existing tests still pass
TypeScript build is clean
notes: Root cause: drive.ts passes absolute paths directly to gws --upload. gws validates that the upload path must be within the current directory. Fix: set cwd in execa options to dirname(localPath) and pass only the basename as --upload. This must be applied to uploadAsDoc, uploadAsSheet, and updateSheet. Alternatively, use relative paths from cwd.
close_reason: Fixed: all three upload functions now pass cwd: dirname(localPath) to execa and use basename for --upload. Tests pass (28/28), build clean.

title: Inventory CSV columns are empty or have wrong default values
description:
The _inventory.csv produced by the crawler has several columns that are always empty or contain incorrect placeholder values:

1. Statut_HTTP is always 0 — the wget stderr parsers in download.ts use regexes that do not match the actual output format of 'wget --quiet --debug --server-response', so the status code is never extracted.

2. Date_modifiee is always 'missing-value' — because the Last-Modified header is never parsed (same parser failure), extractMeta() receives undefined headers and falls back to the placeholder.

3. Noindex is blank for normal pages — csv-stringify serializes boolean false as an empty string, so pages without a noindex tag show nothing instead of 'no'.

4. crawl_status is always empty — processPage() never assigns a value to this field on the InventoryRow.

Date_modifiee shows parsed YYYYMMDD from Last-Modified header when present, and 'missing-value' only when truly absent

crawl_status contains 'done' for every successfully processed row
All existing tests pass

Test with a real wget invocation to capture stderr. (2) meta.ts — Noindex field should be typed as string ('yes'|'no') or handled at serialization time in inventory.ts. title: BUG: sanitizeHtml strips content containers via overly broad class matching
description:
## Root cause

`sanitizeHtml` in `src/packages/crawler/src/sanitize.ts` uses overly broad CSS attribute-substring selectors to remove elements:

```ts
const selector = `[class*="${keyword}" i], [id*="${keyword}" i]`;
```

The `*=` operator matches any substring. For keyword `nav`, this matches classes like `innovative`, `main-nav-wrapper`, `navigation-panel` — any class containing the letters "nav" anywhere. If the target website wraps its main content in an element whose class happens to contain a removal keyword (e.g., `x-navigation-content`, `site-header-main`), the entire content block is silently stripped.

For `standredekamouraska.ca/espace-citoyen/urbanisme/`, the extracted text is only the page title repeated, suggesting the main content container was removed by `sanitizeHtml` while title elements (in `<head>` or a different container) survived.

## Impact
- Pages appear empty or title-only in output `.txt` files
- Substantial content loss on websites with aggressive class naming
- User sees incomplete crawl results

## Files affected
- `src/packages/crawler/src/sanitize.ts`
- `src/packages/crawler/src/convert.ts` (if issue is in htmlToText instead)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `sanitizeHtml` uses word-boundary or exact matching for class/id removal keywords instead of substring matching
- [ ] Content from `standredekamouraska.ca/espace-citoyen/urbanisme/` is fully extracted (headings, lists, paragraphs, links) — not just title
- [ ] `mrckamouraska.com/services/developpement-du-territoire/developpement-culturel/` continues to extract correctly (regression test)
- [ ] `cd src/packages/crawler && pnpm build` exits 0

## Test plan
- `cd src/packages/crawler && pnpm build`
- Add a unit test that feeds the provided HTML snippet through `sanitizeHtml` + `htmlToText` and verifies the extracted text contains "Permis", "Demande d'un permis de construction", and paragraph text about "îlots déstructurés"
- Manual: re-crawl both URLs and verify output `.txt` files contain expected content
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-04-26):

The <body> tag of standredekamouraska.ca has class="x-navbar-fixed-top-active".

sanitizeHtml's removal loop uses  which matches ANY class containing the substring "nav". Since "navbar" contains "nav", the <body> element itself is matched and removed — destroying the entire page content.

What survives:
- <head> elements (<title>, <meta og:title>) → htmlToText fallback iterates these
- Result: title repeated 3x, zero body content

The content IS in the sanitized HTML before the loop (confirmed: "Permis", "îlots déstructurés", "MRC: Laura" all FOUND). The removal loop strips it all by killing <body>.

Fix: class/id keyword removal must exclude structural container tags (<body>, <html>, <main>) from matching.
close_reason: Fixed: added :not(body):not(html):not(main) to class/id keyword selectors in sanitizeHtml. <body> with class containing nav/menu/etc is no longer removed. Verified: standredekamouraska.ca content extracts fully (4840 chars vs 150 before). Build passes.

title: BUG: URLs with hash fragments crawled as distinct pages
description:
## Root cause

URLs with hash fragments (e.g., `https://example.com/page#section`) are treated as distinct pages by the crawler, but fragments are client-side only — they resolve to the same page. The fragment is never sent to the server.

`discoverDomainUrls` / `discoverFolderUrls` → `extractLinks` uses `new URL(href, base).href` which preserves the fragment. So discovered URLs include fragments.

`crawl()` adds full URLs (with fragments) to `doneUrls` Set and checks `doneUrls.has(url)` for resume. Two URLs differing only by fragment are treated as different.

`processPage()` downloads the URL as-is, including the fragment, causing redundant fetches of the same page.

## Impact
- Same page fetched multiple times (once per fragment variant)
- Duplicate rows in inventory (same content, different URL keys)
- Wasted bandwidth and processing time

## Files affected
- `src/packages/crawler/src/crawl.ts`
- `src/packages/crawler/src/discover.ts` (optional: normalize in extractLinks)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] URLs with fragments (`#section`) are normalized to fragment-less form before deduplication and crawling
- [ ] `doneUrls` Set uses normalized URLs
- [ ] Inventory upserts use normalized URLs as keys
- [ ] `discoverDomainUrls` / `discoverFolderUrls` return deduplicated fragment-less URLs
- [ ] `cd src/packages/crawler && pnpm build` exits 0

## Test plan
- `cd src/packages/crawler && pnpm build`
- Manual: crawl a page with multiple `#fragment` links, verify each target page is only processed once
close_reason: Fixed: added stripHash() helper in crawl.ts and discover.ts. URLs with #fragments are normalized before dedup (doneUrls), inventory keys, and link extraction. Build passes.

title: BUG: Crawler writes inventory to wrong path in page/list mode — resume broken, rows lost
description:
## Problem

In `crawl()`, the inventory path is computed as:
```ts
const resolvedInventoryPath = join(outputDir, `${client}_${project}`, domain, "_inventory.csv");
```

For `page` and `list` modes, `domain` is the empty string "", so the path resolves to:
`{outputDir}/{client}_{project}/_inventory.csv`

But in `processPage()`, the inventory path is computed as:
```ts
const domainDir = join(outputDir, `${client}_${project}`, pageDomain);
const inventoryPath = join(domainDir, "_inventory.csv");
```

where `pageDomain` is derived from `new URL(url).hostname`. So the path resolves to:
`{outputDir}/{client}_{project}/{hostname}/_inventory.csv`

## Impact

1. **Resume is broken**: `crawl()` loads done URLs from the wrong file (flat path, no hostname), so already-crawled URLs are NOT skipped.
2. **Inventory rows are split across two files**: `crawl()` initializes headers at the flat path; `processPage()` upserts rows at the hostname path. The final inventory is incomplete.
3. **ENOENT crash on first run**: `writeInventory()` in @full-content-inventory/shared does not create parent directories. If the `{client}_{project}/` directory does not exist yet, the initial `writeInventory(resolvedInventoryPath, [])` in `crawl()` throws ENOENT before any page is processed.

## Root cause

`crawl()` uses the old pre-20n logic where `domain` was set only for domain/folder modes. After 20n fixed `processPage()` to derive hostname per-URL, `crawl()` was never updated to match.

## Files affected
- `src/packages/crawler/src/crawl.ts`
- `src/packages/shared/src/inventory.ts` (optional: add directory creation)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `crawl()\'s resume check and initial inventory write use the same path as `processPage()` for all crawl modes
- [ ] Parent directories are created before the first inventory write
- [ ] All crawl modes (domain, folder, page, list) produce inventory at `{outputDir}/{client}_{project}/{hostname}/_inventory.csv`
- [ ] Existing tests still pass; build exits 0
close_reason: Fixed by worker: (1) domain extracted unconditionally from urls[0] for all modes so resolvedInventoryPath matches processPage(); (2) ensureDirForFile() added before writeInventory() to prevent ENOENT on first run; build passes

title: Non-domain crawl modes dump all URLs into same directory — missing domain segregation
description:
## Context

Discovered during validation of full-content-inventory-integrated-hv7 (Fix output path structure and homepage.txt mapping).

In `crawl()` in `src/packages/crawler/src/crawl.ts`, the `domain` variable is only set when `mode === 'domain'` (extracted from the seed URL hostname). For `mode === 'page'` or `mode === 'list'`, `domain` remains the empty string `''`.

This means `processPage()` constructs `domainDir = join(outputDir, \`${client}_${project}\`, domain)` which resolves to `{outputDir}/{client}_{project}/` with no domain subdirectory.

## Question

If a user passes multiple URLs from different domains in page/list mode (e.g. `--url https://a.com/page1 --url https://b.com/page2`), both `.txt` files will be written to the same flat directory `{outputDir}/c_p/`. Their relative paths may collide (e.g. both `/about.html` → `about.txt`), causing overwrites.

**Is this intentional?** Should page/list mode also derive a per-URL domain directory, or is the current flat-directory behavior by design?

## Potential fix (if deemed a bug)

In `processPage()`, derive `domain` from the URL being processed rather than relying on the `domain` parameter passed from `crawl()`:

```ts
const urlDomain = new URL(url).hostname;
const domainDir = join(outputDir, `${client}_${project}`, urlDomain);
```

This would ensure every URL lands in `{outputDir}/{client}_{project}/{hostname}/` regardless of crawl mode.

title: Fix Unicode normalization gaps in sanitizeText() before injection pattern matching
description:
## Why this exists

sanitizeText() in src/packages/crawler/src/injection.ts has three security gaps that allow prompt injection payloads to bypass keyword matching:

**Gap 1 — unidecode applied to full text content (not just file paths)**
injection.ts:171 calls unidecode(result) on the entire page text. specs.md FR-5 only mandates unidecode for file-system path naming. Applied to content, it silently destroys legitimate French/multilingual text (é → e, à → a), degrading .txt files fed to ai-summarizer. The fix must preserve content fidelity while still normalizing for injection detection.

**Gap 2 — Homoglyph map is Cyrillic-only; Greek is only caught by unidecode**
The explicit HOMOGLYPH_MAP (injection.ts:64–103) covers ~16 Cyrillic lookalikes. Greek has 14+ visually identical Latin lookalikes (Α/A, Β/B, Ε/E, Η/H, Ι/I, Κ/K, Μ/M, Ν/N, Ο/O, Ρ/P, Τ/T, Υ/Y, Χ/X, ο/o). Currently only caught because unidecode runs afterward — pulling unidecode from content sanitization (Gap 1 fix) exposes this.

**Gap 3 — Missing invisible character classes**
INVISIBLE_CHARS (injection.ts:31–58) misses:
- Unicode Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F): documented LLM invisible-text injection vector
- Variation selectors (U+FE00–U+FE0F): alter glyph rendering, bypass keyword matching
- Fullwidth Latin (U+FF01–U+FF5E): e.g. ｉｇｎｏｒｅ bypasses word-boundary regex
- Mathematical alphanumerics (U+1D400–U+1D7FF): 𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐞 styled but not matched

## What needs to be done

1. Replace the unidecode-on-content approach with Unicode NFKC normalization (String.prototype.normalize('NFKC')) applied before injection pattern matching. NFKC collapses fullwidth, mathematical variants, and compatibility forms into base characters without destroying accented letters.
2. Add Greek homoglyph entries to HOMOGLYPH_MAP (or rely on NFKC + a separate confusables pass).
3. Extend INVISIBLE_CHARS to cover Unicode Tags block, variation selectors, and any remaining formatting characters.
4. Keep unidecode usage isolated to the file-path slug generation (convert.ts / crawl.ts), not in sanitizeText().

title: Implement domain crawl mode: sitemap discovery + BFS fallback
description:
## Why this exists

Domain crawl mode (specs FR-16) is entirely unimplemented. When --mode domain is passed, the crawler should discover all URLs on the seed domain via robots.txt → Sitemap: → sitemap XML, with a fallback to BFS link-following if no sitemap exists. This is the primary crawl mode for full-site inventories.

## What needs to be done

1. Create src/packages/crawler/src/discover.ts with discoverDomainUrls(seedUrl, options): Promise<string[]>.
2. The function fetches {seedOrigin}/robots.txt, parses Sitemap: directives, fetches each sitemap, collects all <url><loc> entries; recurses one level into <sitemapindex> entries.
3. If no URLs are found via sitemap, falls back to BFS: extract <a href> links from seed page HTML, filter to same hostname, enqueue unvisited with a Set<string> guard.
4. Replace the 'mode not yet implemented' stub in crawl() for mode='domain' with a call to discoverDomainUrls().

title: Add request delay and --mode flag to crawl() and CLI
description:
## Why this exists

crawl() has no configurable request delay between page fetches — specs require a minimum 500ms default (Non-Functional Requirements, Performance). CrawlOptions has no mode field and the CLI has no --mode flag, which will be required when domain and folder crawl modes are implemented. Without this scaffolding, subsequent tasks cannot introduce mode-specific behaviour.

## What needs to be done

1. Add delay?: number (default 500) and mode: 'domain' | 'folder' | 'page' | 'list' to CrawlOptions interface.
2. In crawl() loop, sleep delay ms between processPage() calls (not before the first call).
3. When mode is 'domain' or 'folder', log 'mode not yet implemented' and exit(1) as a placeholder until task-004/005.
4. Add --mode and --delay flags to CLI; validate mode value against the enum; validate delay is a positive integer.
